questions.q: In a school cricket match, batter P scored 42 runs off 28 balls. The scorer lists three other batters. Whose runs : balls ratio is NOT proportional to P's?
questions.a: R: 66 runs off 45 balls

questions.q:
School X has 18 teachers for 630 students. School Y has 22 teachers for 770 students.
(a) Use cross multiplication to test whether the two teacher : student ratios are proportional.
(b) School Z has 24 teachers and wants its teacher : student ratio to be proportional to School X's. How many students should it have?
s: Part (a): both cross products 13,860, so the ratios are proportional
Part (b): sets 18 : 630 :: 24 : x and gets 840 students

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 12 : 18 and 10 : 15 are proportional, because 12 x 15 and 18 x 10 are both 180.
Statement 2: 8 : 5 and 11 : 8 are proportional, because in each ratio the second term is 3 less than the first.
Statement 3: Since 4 : 6 :: 10 : 15, the statement 4 : 10 :: 6 : 15 is also true.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q:
A school canteen in Madurai makes a lemon-mint drink. Its tested recipe uses 3 litres of lemon syrup for every 8 litres of water. The record book for four days shows:
Monday: 4.5 L syrup, 12 L water
Tuesday: 6 L syrup, 15 L water
Wednesday: 3.6 L syrup, 9.6 L water
Thursday: 5 L syrup, 14 L water
(a) On which days was the drink proportional to the tested recipe?
(b) Of the two other days, on which day was the drink stronger than the recipe (more syrup for its water)? Show the check.
(c) On Friday 20 L of water is available. How much syrup is needed?
(d) Thursday's jug is still in the fridge. Nothing may be poured away, water is plentiful, and only 0.2 L of syrup is left in the kitchen. Can Thursday's jug be brought to the tested recipe today? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Monday: 4.5 x 8 = 36 = 12 x 3; Wednesday: 3.6 x 8 = 28.8 = 9.6 x 3. So Monday and Wednesday. (b) Tuesday: 6 x 8 = 48 against 15 x 3 = 45, so the syrup side is bigger and Tuesday's drink was stronger. (Thursday: 5 x 8 = 40 against 14 x 3 = 42, so Thursday's was weaker.) (c) 3 : 8 :: x : 20 gives 8x = 60, x = 7.5 L of syrup. (d) No. Thursday's drink is too weak, so only syrup can fix it; adding water would make it weaker still. For 14 L of water the syrup needed is 3 x 14 / 8 = 5.25 L, so 5.25 - 5 = 0.25 L of syrup must be added, but only 0.2 L is left.
s: Part (a): Monday and Wednesday, with equal cross products
Part (b): Tuesday, since 48 is more than 45
Part (c): 7.5 L of syrup
Part (d): No, since 0.25 L of syrup is needed but only 0.2 L is left (water would only weaken it)

questions.q: A juice stall mixes mango pulp and water in the ratio 3 : 5. Which of these jugs will taste the same as the stall's drink?
questions.a: 4.5 litres of pulp with 7.5 litres of water
o: 4.5 litres of pulp with 7.5 litres of water
5 litres of pulp with 7 litres of water
6 litres of pulp with 8 litres of water
7.5 litres of pulp with 4.5 litres of water

questions.q: Meera claims: 'If two batters are mixed in proportional ratios and I pour them into one big vessel, the combined batter is still proportional to each of them.' Test her claim with a 6 : 3 batter and a 4 : 2 batter (rice : urad dal), then with a 9 : 4 batter and an 18 : 8 batter. Is Meera right? Give a reason that works for any such pair.
questions.a: Yes, Meera is right. 6 : 3 and 4 : 2 combine to 10 : 5, and 10 x 3 = 30 = 5 x 6, so 10 : 5 :: 6 : 3. 9 : 4 and 18 : 8 combine to 27 : 12, and 27 x 4 = 108 = 12 x 9, so 27 : 12 :: 9 : 4. Reason: if the second batter is k times the first in both terms, the combined batter is (1 + k) times the first in both terms, so both terms change by the same factor.
s: Combines 6 : 3 and 4 : 2 into 10 : 5 and checks the cross products
Combines 9 : 4 and 18 : 8 into 27 : 12 and checks the cross products
States the claim is right, with the same-factor reason

questions.q: True or False: The ratios 0.6 : 1.5 and 4 : 10 cannot be proportional, because one ratio has decimal terms and the other has whole-number terms. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. Cross multiplying, 0.6 x 10 = 6 and 1.5 x 4 = 6. The products are equal, so 0.6 : 1.5 :: 4 : 10. Whether the terms are decimals does not matter; only the cross products do.
s: States False
Shows 0.6 x 10 = 1.5 x 4 = 6, so the ratios are proportional

questions.q: A cycle-repair shop mixes kerosene and oil in the ratio 7 : 2 to clean chains. To keep the mixture proportional when it uses 3 litres of oil, it needs ___ litres of kerosene. (Write the number as a decimal.)

A garage mixes petrol and engine oil for two-stroke scooters. The maker's chart says petrol : oil = 25 : 1. Four cans are found on the shelf:
Can P: 5 L petrol, 0.2 L oil
Can Q: 7.5 L petrol, 0.25 L oil
Can R: 3 L petrol, 0.12 L oil
Can S: 10 L petrol, 0.5 L oil
(a) Test each can against 25 : 1 using cross multiplication.
(b) Which can has too much oil for its petrol?
(c) How much oil must be added to Can Q to correct it?
(d) Oil cannot be taken out of Can S. How much petrol must be added to correct it?
(e) Explain why checking 'the petrol is 25 times the oil' is the same test as cross multiplying.
questions.a: (a) For petrol : oil = p : q against 25 : 1, compare p x 1 with q x 25. P: 5 and 5, proportional. Q: 7.5 and 6.25, not. R: 3 and 3, proportional. S: 10 and 12.5, not. (b) Can S, because q x 25 = 12.5 is more than its 10 L of petrol. (c) Q needs 7.5 / 25 = 0.3 L of oil, so add 0.3 - 0.25 = 0.05 L. (d) S needs 0.5 x 25 = 12.5 L of petrol, so add 12.5 - 10 = 2.5 L. (e) Cross multiplying p : q with 25 : 1 compares p x 1 with q x 25, that is, p with 25 times q; so the two checks are the same comparison.
s: Part (a): P and R proportional, Q and S not, with the cross products
Part (b): Can S has too much oil
Parts (c) and (d): add 0.05 L oil to Q and 2.5 L petrol to S
Part (e): explains that p x 1 = q x 25 is the same as petrol = 25 x oil

questions.q: A jam maker's tested batch used 2.4 kg of sugar with 6 kg of fruit. A bigger batch uses 10 kg of fruit. How much sugar keeps the bigger batch proportional to the tested one?
questions.a: 4 kg

questions.q:
To test whether 5 : 8 and 15 : 24 are proportional, Rohit works out 5 x 15 = 75 and 8 x 24 = 192, and writes 'not proportional'.
(a) What is the mistake in his method?
(b) Do the test correctly and state the result.
questions.a: (a) He multiplied the two first terms together and the two second terms together. Cross multiplication multiplies the first term of one ratio by the second term of the other. (b) 5 x 24 = 120 and 8 x 15 = 120. The products are equal, so 5 : 8 :: 15 : 24.
s: Part (a): names the wrong pairing of terms
Part (b): 5 x 24 = 8 x 15 = 120, so the ratios are proportional

questions.q: Shop P sells 6 notebooks for Rs 45. Shop Q sells 10 of the same notebooks for Rs 75. Which conclusion about notebooks : rupees is correct?
questions.a: Proportional, since 6 x 75 = 45 x 10
o: Not proportional, since 6 x 45 is not 10 x 75
Not proportional, since Shop Q charges Rs 30 more

questions.q:
A chapati recipe card says flour : water = 5 : 3 by weight.
(a) Asha uses 1.2 kg of flour. How many grams of water keep her dough proportional to the card?
(b) Binu weighs 750 g of flour and 450 g of water. Test his dough against 5 : 3.
(c) Chitra mixes 2 kg of flour with 1,200 g of water and writes '2 : 1,200 is nothing like 5 : 3, so my dough is wrong.' Find her mistake and test her dough correctly.
questions.a: (a) 5 : 3 :: 1.2 : x gives 5x = 3.6, x = 0.72 kg = 720 g of water. (b) 750 x 3 = 2,250 and 450 x 5 = 2,250. The products are equal, so his dough is proportional. (c) She compared kilograms with grams; both terms of a ratio must be in the same unit. 2 kg = 2,000 g, and 2,000 x 3 = 6,000 = 1,200 x 5, so 2,000 : 1,200 :: 5 : 3 and her dough is right.
s: Part (a): 0.72 kg = 720 g of water
Part (b): both cross products 2,250, so proportional
Part (c): names the mixed units and shows 2,000 : 1,200 :: 5 : 3

questions.q:
Match each ratio in Column A with the ratio in Column B that it is proportional to.
Column A: (1) 16 : 24 (2) 4.5 : 3 (3) 0.8 : 2 (4) 2.5 : 7.5
Column B: (a) 2 : 5 (b) 3 : 2 (c) 2 : 3 (d) 1 : 3
Using a recipe as your example, explain why 'the difference between the two terms stays the same' is not a test of proportionality, while 'the cross products are equal' is.
questions.a: Example: idli batter 2 : 1 (rice : dal) and 4 : 3. Both have a difference of 1, but 2 x 3 = 6 and 1 x 4 = 4, so they are not proportional: the second batter has much more dal for its rice and would taste different. Proportional quantities change by the same factor, not by the same amount; equal cross products show the same factor (2 : 1 and 4 : 2 give 2 x 2 = 1 x 4).
s: Gives an example with the same difference but unequal cross products
Explains that proportionality means the same factor, which equal cross products show

questions.q:
A housing society in Pune buys water from tankers. The secretary notes two loads from each supplier:
Supplier X: 6,000 L for Rs 1,500 and 10,000 L for Rs 2,500
Supplier Y: 5,000 L for Rs 1,200 and 8,000 L for Rs 2,000
Supplier Z: 4,000 L for Rs 1,100 and 12,000 L for Rs 3,300
(a) Whose two prices are proportional to the litres (one fixed rate)? Use cross multiplication.
(b) For the other supplier, which of the two loads gives more litres for each rupee? Show the check.
(c) The society needs 9,000 L. What would X and Z charge for it at their own fixed rates?
(d) Instead of one 9,000 L load from X, the society could buy Y's 5,000 L load and Z's 4,000 L load. Which choice costs less, and by how much?
questions.a: (a) X: 6,000 x 2,500 = 1,50,00,000 = 1,500 x 10,000, proportional. Y: 5,000 x 2,000 = 1,00,00,000 but 1,200 x 8,000 = 96,00,000, not proportional. Z: 4,000 x 3,300 = 1,32,00,000 = 1,100 x 12,000, proportional. So X and Z. (b) Comparing 5,000 : 1,200 with 8,000 : 2,000, the product 5,000 x 2,000 = 1,00,00,000 is bigger than 1,200 x 8,000 = 96,00,000, so the 5,000 L load gives more litres for each rupee. (c) X: 6,000 : 1,500 :: 9,000 : x gives x = Rs 2,250. Z: 4,000 : 1,100 :: 9,000 : x gives x = Rs 2,475. (d) Y's 5,000 L costs Rs 1,200 and Z's 4,000 L costs Rs 1,100, together Rs 2,300. X's single load costs Rs 2,250, so X is cheaper by Rs 50.
s: Part (a): X and Z proportional, Y not, with the cross products
Part (b): Y's 5,000 L load gives more litres per rupee
Part (c): X Rs 2,250 and Z Rs 2,475
Part (d): X's single load, cheaper by Rs 50 than Rs 2,300

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Adding 1 cup of rice and 1 cup of urad dal to a batter made with 6 cups of rice and 3 cups of urad dal keeps it proportional to 6 : 3.
Reason (R): Two ratios are proportional only when both terms change by the same factor.
questions.a: A is false but R is true
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.q: Write a real-life situation about two mixtures that the statement 4 : 7 :: 12 : 21 describes. Use cross multiplication to show the statement is correct, and then change one of the four numbers so that the two mixtures would no longer taste the same.
questions.a: Example: one jug of tea uses 4 spoons of sugar for 7 cups of milk; a bigger pot uses 12 spoons of sugar for 21 cups of milk. Check: 4 x 21 = 84 and 7 x 12 = 84, equal, so 4 : 7 :: 12 : 21. Changing 21 to 20 gives 4 x 20 = 80, not 84, so the pot would be sweeter and the mixtures would no longer be proportional. (Any correct situation and any valid change earn the marks.)
s: Writes a situation in which both ratios compare the same two quantities in the same order
Shows 4 x 21 = 7 x 12 = 84
Changes one number and shows the cross products are now unequal

questions.q: A photocopy shop charged Rs 36 for 48 pages. At the same rate, a student paid Rs 51. How many pages were copied?
questions.a: 68 pages

questions.q:
Tea stall A uses 2 spoons of tea leaves for 300 ml of water. Stall B writes its recipe as water : tea leaves = 450 : 3 (ml to spoons).
(a) Rewrite Stall B's ratio in the same order as Stall A's.
(b) Test whether the two recipes are proportional.
questions.a: (a) Tea leaves : water = 3 : 450 for Stall B (Stall A is 2 : 300). (b) 2 x 450 = 900 and 300 x 3 = 900. The products are equal, so 2 : 300 :: 3 : 450 and the recipes are proportional.
s: Part (a): writes Stall B as 3 : 450 in the order tea leaves : water
Part (b): 2 x 450 = 300 x 3 = 900, so proportional

questions.q:
A class records the height of a bean plant: on day 4 it is 6 cm, on day 6 it is 9 cm, on day 10 it is 15 cm and on day 14 it is 20 cm.
(a) Test height : days for day 4 against day 6, and day 4 against day 10.
(b) Test day 4 against day 14.
(c) If the relationship seen up to day 10 held on day 8, what height would the plant have had on day 8?
(d) If exactly one height in the record were changed so that the whole record became proportional, which height would it be and what value? Explain why changing any other height cannot work.
(e) The teacher confirms that 20 cm on day 14 was measured correctly. Can the class say the plant's height is proportional to the number of days over all 14 days? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 6 : 4 and 9 : 6: 6 x 6 = 36 = 4 x 9; 6 : 4 and 15 : 10: 6 x 10 = 60 = 4 x 15. Both proportional. (b) 6 : 4 and 20 : 14: 6 x 14 = 84 but 4 x 20 = 80, not proportional. (c) 6 : 4 :: h : 8 gives 4h = 48, h = 12 cm. (d) The day 14 height, changed to 6 x 14 / 4 = 21 cm. The other three readings already agree with one another (1.5 cm for each day), so changing any one of them would break that agreement and day 14 would still not fit. (e) No. A proportional relationship must hold for every pair of readings; the correct day 14 reading breaks it, so the height is proportional to the days only up to day 10.
s: Part (a): both cross-product checks equal
Part (b): 84 against 80, not proportional
Part (c): 12 cm
Part (d): the day 14 height, which should be 21 cm, since the other three agree
Part (e): No, because one pair fails

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: On a map with RF 1 : 25,00,000, a distance of 1 cm stands for 250 km on the ground.
Statement 2: If two maps of India have RFs 1 : 40,00,000 and 1 : 80,00,000, the Delhi to Agra distance measured on the second map is half of that measured on the first.
Statement 3: The distance worked out from the RF is the geographical distance, which can differ from the distance by road.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: On a map of Karnataka with RF 1 : 40,00,000, Bengaluru and Mysuru are 3.5 cm apart. What is the geographical distance between them?
questions.a: 140 km

questions.q:
Sanya reads a map with RF 1 : 5,00,000 and measures 8 cm between two villages. She writes: 'Actual distance = 8 / 5,00,000 km.'
(a) What is wrong with her working?
(b) Find the correct geographical distance in km.
questions.a: (a) The RF says 1 cm on the map stands for 5,00,000 cm on the ground, so the map distance must be multiplied by 5,00,000, not divided; and the result is in cm, not km. (b) 8 x 5,00,000 = 40,00,000 cm = 40,00,000 / 1,00,000 km = 40 km.
s: Part (a): says she should multiply, and that the result is in cm

questions.q:
The district office in Wayanad is choosing a site for a new health centre. Its planning map has RF 1 : 2,00,000. The map distances measured by the clerk are:
Site P: 6.8 cm from village V, 5.5 cm from the old hospital H
Site Q: 8.1 cm from village V, 7 cm from the old hospital H
Site R: 5.9 cm from village V, 4.8 cm from the old hospital H
The rule is that the centre must be within 15 km (geographical) of village V and at least 10 km from the old hospital H.
(a) Find the geographical distance of each site from village V.
(b) Find the geographical distance of each site from the old hospital H.
(c) Which site meets both conditions? Name the condition each other site fails.
(d) The office would like a site closer to village V than the one in (c). It may relax ONE rule by 1 km: either 'within 16 km of V' or 'at least 9 km from H'. Which rule should it relax, and which site would it then choose? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 1 cm stands for 2,00,000 cm = 2 km. P: 6.8 x 2 = 13.6 km, Q: 8.1 x 2 = 16.2 km, R: 5.9 x 2 = 11.8 km. (b) P: 5.5 x 2 = 11 km, Q: 7 x 2 = 14 km, R: 4.8 x 2 = 9.6 km. (c) Site P: it is 13.6 km from V (within 15 km) and 11 km from H (at least 10 km). Q fails the first condition (16.2 km from V) and R fails the second (only 9.6 km from H). (d) Relaxing the V rule to 16 km does not help, since Q is 16.2 km from V. Relaxing the H rule to 9 km lets in R (11.8 km from V, 9.6 km from H), which is closer to V than P (13.6 km). So relax the hospital rule and choose Site R.
s: Part (a): 13.6 km, 16.2 km and 11.8 km from V
Part (b): 11 km, 14 km and 9.6 km from H
Part (c): Site P, with Q failing the V rule and R the H rule
Part (d): relax the hospital rule to 9 km and choose Site R (11.8 km from V)

questions.q: On a map with RF 1 : 45,00,000, two towns are 18 mm apart. What is the geographical distance between them?
questions.a: 81 km, since 18 mm is 1.8 cm and 1 cm stands for 45 km
o: 81 km, since 18 mm is 1.8 cm and 1 cm stands for 45 km
810 km, since 18 mm is read as 18 cm and 1 cm stands for 45 km
8.1 km, since 18 mm is 1.8 cm and 1 cm stands for 4.5 km
45 km, since the 1 in the RF always stands for 1 cm on the map

questions.q: True or False: Two maps of Gujarat have RFs 1 : 20,00,000 and 1 : 50,00,000. Ahmedabad and Rajkot are 10 cm apart on the first map, so they will be 4 cm apart on the second map. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. On the first map 1 cm stands for 20 km, so the geographical distance is 10 x 20 = 200 km. On the second map 1 cm stands for 50 km, so the map distance is 200 / 50 = 4 cm.
s: States True
Finds 200 km from the first map and 200 / 50 = 4 cm on the second

questions.q: A trekking map has RF 1 : 50,000. A straight stretch of path measures 74 mm on the map, so its geographical length is ___ km. (Write the number in digits.)

Delhi and Jaipur are taken to be 240 km apart (geographical distance). Kiran says: 'On a map with RF 1 : 10,00,000 they are 24 cm apart. On a map with RF 1 : 30,00,000 they are 3 cm closer, because its second term is 3 times bigger.' Check both parts of Kiran's statement and give your verdict.
questions.a: Kiran is partly right. 240 km = 2,40,00,000 cm, and 2,40,00,000 / 10,00,000 = 24 cm, so the first part is correct. On the second map, 2,40,00,000 / 30,00,000 = 8 cm, which is one-third of 24 cm, not 3 cm less (it is 16 cm closer). When the second term is 3 times bigger, the map distance is divided by 3; it does not drop by 3.
s: Checks the first map: 24 cm, correct
Finds 8 cm on the second map
Verdict partly right: the map distance is divided by 3, not reduced by 3

questions.q:
The geographical distance from Kanyakumari to Srinagar is taken as 3,000 km.
(a) How far apart are they on a map of India with RF 1 : 2,50,00,000?
(b) On a classroom wall map they are 60 cm apart. Find the RF of the wall map.
(c) How many times as long does every distance look on the wall map as on the first map? Show that the two RFs give the same answer.
s: Part (a): 12 cm
Part (c): 5 times, from both the distances and the RFs

questions.q: A school's site plan is drawn at RF 1 : 2,000. The playground is 84 m long. How long is it on the plan?
questions.a: 4.2 cm

questions.q:
A town planner must show a straight canal 4.5 km long on a map drawn at RF 1 : 25,000.
(a) Write 4.5 km in centimetres.
(b) Find the length of the canal on the map.
s: Part (b): divides by 25,000 to get 18 cm

questions.q:
Three students find the geographical distance between the same two cities, each using a different map.
Priya: map with RF 1 : 60,00,000, measured 5.2 cm
Qasim: map with RF 1 : 25,00,000, measured 13.6 cm
Rekha: map with RF 1 : 1,00,00,000, measured 3.1 cm
(a) Find the distance each student gets, in km.
(b) Whose result does not agree with the other two? Suggest what most likely went wrong.
(c) Taking the distance as 312 km, what should that student have measured?
(d) A ruler reading can be off by 1 mm (0.1 cm). How many km does a 1 mm slip cause on Qasim's map and on Rekha's map?
(e) Qasim's odd result in (b) was a reading slip, not a fault in his map. Which of the three maps gives the most trustworthy distance from a careful ruler reading? Justify using part (d).
questions.a: (a) Priya: 5.2 x 60 = 312 km. Qasim: 13.6 x 25 = 340 km. Rekha: 3.1 x 100 = 310 km. (b) Qasim's 340 km is far from 312 km and 310 km, so he most likely misread the ruler (by about 1 cm). (c) 312 / 25 = 12.48 cm. (d) On Qasim's map 1 cm stands for 25 km, so 0.1 cm stands for 2.5 km; on Rekha's map 1 cm stands for 100 km, so 0.1 cm stands for 10 km. (e) Qasim's map (1 : 25,00,000), because the same 1 mm slip changes the distance by only 2.5 km there, against 6 km on Priya's map and 10 km on Rekha's.
s: Part (a): 312 km, 340 km and 310 km
Part (b): picks Qasim's result as the odd one, with a likely measuring slip
Part (c): 12.48 cm
Part (d): 2.5 km on Qasim's map and 10 km on Rekha's
Part (e): the 1 : 25,00,000 map, because a slip costs the fewest km

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A distance of 6 cm on a map with RF 1 : 20,00,000 and a distance of 3 cm on a map with RF 1 : 40,00,000 stand for the same geographical distance.
Reason (R): Multiplying the map distance by the second term of the RF gives the actual distance in the same unit as the map distance.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q: A map gives its scale only as RF 1 : 60,00,000, with no unit written. Explain why the RF needs no unit, and use your reason to find the geographical distance shown by 5 mm on this map.
questions.a: Both terms of the RF are in the same unit, whatever that unit is: 1 unit on the map stands for 60,00,000 of the same unit on the ground. So 5 mm on the map stands for 5 x 60,00,000 = 3,00,00,000 mm = 30,000 m = 30 km.
s: Explains that both terms are in the same unit, so any unit can be used

questions.q: The geographical distance between Delhi and Kolkata is taken as 1,300 km. Anu wants to draw both cities on a single sheet whose longest straight line is 30 cm, using RF 1 : 40,00,000. Show that this cannot be done, and decide which of the RFs 1 : 50,00,000 and 1 : 60,00,000 gives the bigger drawing that still fits.
questions.a: 1,300 km = 13,00,00,000 cm. At 1 : 40,00,000 the map distance is 13,00,00,000 / 40,00,000 = 32.5 cm, which is more than 30 cm, so the two cities cannot both fit. At 1 : 50,00,000 it is 26 cm, which fits (and 1 : 60,00,000 gives about 21.7 cm, smaller still). So 1 : 50,00,000 is the RF with the biggest drawing that fits.
s: Converts 1,300 km to 13,00,00,000 cm
Finds 32.5 cm at 1 : 40,00,000 and says it exceeds 30 cm
Finds 26 cm at 1 : 50,00,000 and chooses it

questions.q:
Match each map reading in Column A with the geographical distance in Column B.
Column A: (1) RF 1 : 20,00,000, map distance 4 cm (2) RF 1 : 4,00,000, map distance 5 cm (3) RF 1 : 50,000, map distance 8 cm (4) RF 1 : 80,00,000, map distance 2.5 cm
Column B: (a) 20 km (b) 4 km (c) 200 km (d) 80 km
On a state map, Chennai and Puducherry, 135 km apart (geographical distance), are shown 4.5 cm apart. What is the RF of this map?

Two villages are 6.4 cm apart on a map with RF 1 : 2,50,000.
(a) Find their geographical distance in km.
(b) How far apart would they be on a map with RF 1 : 4,00,000?
(c) The bus route between them is 21 km long. Explain why this is not a mistake.
questions.a: (a) 6.4 x 2,50,000 = 16,00,000 cm = 16 km. (b) On the second map 1 cm stands for 4 km, so 16 / 4 = 4 cm. (c) The RF gives the geographical (straight-line) distance, not the road distance. Roads bend around hills, rivers and towns, so the bus route of 21 km is longer than 16 km.
s: Part (a): 16 km
Part (b): 4 cm
Part (c): explains geographical distance against road distance

questions.q:
A family's map has RF 1 : 20,00,000. Town A and town B are 6.5 cm apart, town B and town C are 8 cm apart, and town A and town C are 12 cm apart (all straight-line distances on the map).
(a) Find the geographical distances AB and BC.
(b) Find the geographical distance AC.
(c) How many km longer is the path A to B to C than the direct distance A to C?
(d) The bus ticket from A to C says the road distance is 275 km. Explain why this is more than your answer to (b).
(e) A cousin's map of the same area has RF 1 : 25,00,000. How far apart are A and C on that map, and does the road distance printed on the bus ticket change? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 1 cm stands for 20 km. AB = 6.5 x 20 = 130 km; BC = 8 x 20 = 160 km. (b) AC = 12 x 20 = 240 km. (c) 130 + 160 = 290 km, which is 290 - 240 = 50 km longer. (d) 240 km is the geographical (straight-line) distance; the road bends, so the road distance of 275 km is longer. (e) 240 km = 2,40,00,000 cm, and 2,40,00,000 / 25,00,000 = 9.6 cm. The ticket still says 275 km: a different RF changes only how big the map is, not the distance on the ground.
s: Part (a): AB = 130 km and BC = 160 km
Part (b): AC = 240 km
Part (c): 50 km longer
Part (d): road distance is longer than the straight-line distance
Part (e): 9.6 cm on the second map; the road distance stays 275 km

questions.q:
Class 8 students in a Bhopal school draw a plan of their classroom at RF 1 : 50. Their table of real lengths and drawn lengths reads:
Room length: real 9 m, drawn 18 cm
Room width: real 7.5 m, drawn 15 cm
Teacher's desk: real 1.5 m, drawn 3.5 cm
Door width: real 1.2 m, drawn (left blank)
(a) Check the room length entry using the RF.
(b) Which other entry in the table is wrong, and what should it be?
(c) Fill in the drawn width of the door.
(d) On the plan, the wall between two windows measures 6.5 cm. The class wants to fix a 2.8 m notice board there, leaving at least 25 cm of wall on each side of it. Can they? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 9 m = 900 cm, and 900 / 50 = 18 cm, so the entry is correct. (b) The desk: 1.5 m = 150 cm, and 150 / 50 = 3 cm, not 3.5 cm. (The width, 750 / 50 = 15 cm, is correct.) (c) 120 / 50 = 2.4 cm. (d) The real wall is 6.5 x 50 = 325 cm = 3.25 m. The board with 25 cm on each side needs 2.8 + 0.25 + 0.25 = 3.3 m, which is more than 3.25 m, so they cannot.
s: Part (a): 900 / 50 = 18 cm, correct
Part (b): the desk entry should be 3 cm
Part (c): 2.4 cm
Part (d): 3.25 m of wall against 3.3 m needed, so it does not fit

questions.q:
(a) Convert 75,00,000 cm to km.
(b) On a map with RF 1 : 75,00,000, Hyderabad and Vijayawada are 3.6 cm apart. Use part (a) to find the geographical distance between them.
questions.a: (a) 1 km = 1,00,000 cm, so 75,00,000 cm = 75 km. (b) Each cm on the map stands for 75 km, so the distance is 3.6 x 75 = 270 km.
s: Part (a): 75 km
Part (b): 3.6 x 75 = 270 km

questions.q: The same two cities, 150 km apart, are 5 cm apart on map X and 3 cm apart on map Y. What are the RFs of the two maps?

For a school mural, the art teacher's 'sunset orange' uses red : yellow : white = 3 : 5 : 2. The store room has 4 L of red, 6 L of yellow and 4 L of white paint.
(a) If every litre of orange must follow the ratio, which colour runs out first?
(b) How many litres of orange can be made from the paint in the store?
(c) How much of each other colour is left over?
(d) The teacher decides instead to use up all the white paint. How many more litres of red and of yellow must be bought?
(e) Red costs Rs 240 a litre and yellow Rs 200 a litre. What do the extra tins in part (d) cost?
questions.a: (a) Litres per part: red 4 / 3 = 1.33..., yellow 6 / 5 = 1.2, white 4 / 2 = 2. Yellow gives the smallest amount per part, so yellow runs out first. (b) 1 part = 1.2 L: red 3.6 L, yellow 6 L, white 2.4 L, total 12 L of orange. (c) Red 4 - 3.6 = 0.4 L and white 4 - 2.4 = 1.6 L are left. (d) All 4 L of white is 2 parts, so 1 part = 2 L: red 6 L, yellow 10 L. Buy 6 - 4 = 2 L of red and 10 - 6 = 4 L of yellow. (e) 2 x 240 + 4 x 200 = 480 + 800 = Rs 1,280.
s: Part (a): yellow, from litres per part
Part (b): 12 L of orange
Part (c): 0.4 L red and 1.6 L white left
Part (d): buy 2 L red and 4 L yellow
Part (e): Rs 1,280

questions.q: Lata's rangoli powder uses red : yellow : white = 5 : 3 : 2. She has 4.5 cups of yellow powder and wants the same colour mix. How much red and white does she need?
questions.a: 7.5 cups of red and 3 cups of white

3 cups of red and 7.5 cups of white

Reason (R): The HCF of 6, 3, 2 and 1 is 1, so 6 : 3 : 2 : 1 is in its simplest form.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q:
A poha recipe uses poha : chopped onion : peanuts = 4 : 3 : 1 (in cups).
(a) Write the amounts for 6 cups of poha.
(b) Gita likes more onion and uses 9 cups of onion with the other amounts of part (a). Write her new ratio in simplest whole-number form and say which term changed by a different factor.
questions.a: (a) 6 cups of poha is 1.5 times 4, so the amounts are 6 : 4.5 : 1.5 cups. (b) Her amounts are 6 : 9 : 1.5. Multiplying by 2 gives 12 : 18 : 3, and dividing by the HCF 3 gives 4 : 6 : 1. Onion went from 4.5 to 9 cups (factor 2) while poha and peanuts stayed the same (factor 1), so it is no longer 4 : 3 : 1.
s: Part (a): 6 : 4.5 : 1.5 cups
Part (b): 4 : 6 : 1, with onion the term that changed by a different factor

questions.q: A tile-grout mix uses cement : fine sand : stone dust : water-proofer = 2 : 5 : 2.5 : 0.5 by weight. If 1.5 kg of water-proofer is used, the whole mix weighs ___ kg. (Write the number in digits.)

A plant nursery in Lucknow fills pots with a mix of soil : compost : cocopeat = 5 : 3 : 2 by weight. The amount of compost it puts in each size of pot is:
Small pot: 0.6 kg of compost
Medium pot: 1.2 kg of compost
Large pot: 2.7 kg of compost
(a) How much soil and how much cocopeat go into a small pot?
(b) What is the total weight of mix in a medium pot?
(c) How many kg more soil does a large pot take than a medium pot?
(d) A customer orders an extra-large pot holding 7 kg of mix in all. How much compost goes into it, and is that more or less than the compost in a large pot?
questions.a: (a) 0.6 kg of compost is 3 parts, so 1 part = 0.2 kg: soil 5 x 0.2 = 1 kg, cocopeat 2 x 0.2 = 0.4 kg. (b) 1 part = 1.2 / 3 = 0.4 kg: soil 2 kg, compost 1.2 kg, cocopeat 0.8 kg, total 4 kg. (c) Large pot: 1 part = 2.7 / 3 = 0.9 kg, soil 4.5 kg. Medium soil is 2 kg, so 2.5 kg more. (d) The terms add to 10, so compost = 7 x 3 / 10 = 2.1 kg. That is 0.6 kg less than the 2.7 kg in a large pot, even though the order is called extra-large.
s: Part (a): 1 kg soil and 0.4 kg cocopeat
Part (b): 4 kg in a medium pot
Part (c): 2.5 kg more soil
Part (d): 2.1 kg of compost, less than the large pot's 2.7 kg

questions.q: Two shops pack festival hampers with sweets : namkeen packets : dry-fruit packets in the same proportion. Shop P's hamper has 6 sweets, 10 namkeen and 4 dry-fruit packets. Shop Q's hamper has 9 sweets. How many namkeen and dry-fruit packets does Shop Q's hamper hold together?

Hari's laddoo recipe uses besan : sugar : ghee = 6 : 4 : 3. He meant to use 1.2 kg of besan, 800 g of sugar and 600 g of ghee, He had already added the planned besan and ghee when he poured in 900 g of sugar by mistake.
(a) Show that his planned amounts followed the ratio.
(b) He cannot take the sugar out. How much more besan and ghee must he add to keep the ratio?
(c) What is the total weight of the corrected mixture?
questions.a: (a) 1,200 / 6 = 200, 800 / 4 = 200 and 600 / 3 = 200 (grams per part), all equal, so the plan followed 6 : 4 : 3. (b) 900 g of sugar is 4 parts, so 1 part = 225 g. Besan = 6 x 225 = 1,350 g and ghee = 3 x 225 = 675 g. He must add 150 g of besan and 75 g of ghee. (c) 1,350 + 900 + 675 = 2,925 g.
s: Part (a): 200 g per part for every ingredient
Part (b): adds 150 g besan and 75 g ghee
Part (c): 2,925 g

questions.q: A dry-fruit pack uses almonds : cashews : raisins = 4 : 3 : 5 by weight. A shop has 1.4 kg of almonds, 1.2 kg of cashews and 2.5 kg of raisins. If every pack follows the ratio, which item runs out first?
questions.a: Almonds, giving only 0.35 kg per part
o: Almonds, giving only 0.35 kg per part
Cashews, because their stock is smallest
Raisins, because 5 is the largest term
None, as 5.1 kg covers all 12 parts

questions.q: True or False: A purple shade uses red : blue : white = 2 : 3 : 5. If Farah doubles the red and the blue but keeps the white the same, the shade stays the same, because red : blue is still 2 : 3. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. The new ratio is 4 : 6 : 5. Comparing term by term with 2 : 3 : 5, 4 / 2 = 2 and 6 / 3 = 2 but 5 / 5 = 1. In a ratio with more than two terms, every term must change by the same factor, so the shade changes (it has less white).
s: States False
Shows the factors 2, 2 and 1 are not all equal, so the ratio is not kept

questions.q: Write a real-life situation about a mixture that the statement 2 : 3 : 5 :: 3 : 4.5 : 7.5 describes. Show that it is a true proportion, and find the total amount of the larger batch in your situation.
questions.a: Example: a fruit punch uses 2 cups of guava juice, 3 cups of orange juice and 5 cups of water; a bigger jug uses 3 cups of guava juice, 4.5 cups of orange juice and 7.5 cups of water. Check: 3 / 2 = 1.5, 4.5 / 3 = 1.5 and 7.5 / 5 = 1.5, the same factor, so it is a true proportion. The larger batch is 3 + 4.5 + 7.5 = 15 cups. (Any situation with three quantities in the same order earns the mark.)
s: Writes a situation with three quantities in a fixed order
Shows every term is multiplied by 1.5
Finds the total of the larger batch, 15 units

questions.q:
A teal paint uses green : blue : white = 4 : 3 : 5. Match each known amount in Column A with the missing amount in Column B.
Column A: (1) green 6 L, so white is (2) blue 4.5 L, so green is (3) white 12 L, so blue is (4) blue 1.2 L, so white is
Column B: (a) 6 L (b) 2 L (c) 7.5 L (d) 7.2 L

(a) Show that 3 : 5 : 8 :: 4.5 : 7.5 : 12 by comparing the ratios term by term.
(b) Riya compares only the first two terms of 3 : 5 : 8 and 6 : 10 : 15 and says the ratios are proportional. Use the method of part (a) to show she is wrong.
questions.a: (a) 4.5 / 3 = 1.5, 7.5 / 5 = 1.5 and 12 / 8 = 1.5. Every term is multiplied by the same factor 1.5, so the ratios are proportional. (b) 6 / 3 = 2 and 10 / 5 = 2, but 15 / 8 = 1.875, not 2. The third terms break the pattern, so the ratios are not proportional; every term must be checked.
s: Part (a): all three quotients are 1.5
Part (b): 15 / 8 is not 2, so not proportional

questions.q: A school orders sports equipment in the ratio footballs : cricket balls : shuttlecocks = 2 : 5 : 12. The office says it already has exactly 14 cricket balls and will order footballs and shuttlecocks to match. Show that this cannot be done with whole footballs, and find which number of cricket balls strictly between 10 and 20 does work, with the matching order.
questions.a: 14 cricket balls are 5 parts, so 1 part = 14 / 5 = 2.8. Footballs would be 2 x 2.8 = 5.6, which is not a whole number, so it cannot be done. The number of cricket balls must make 2 x (balls / 5) whole, which needs a multiple of 5. Between 10 and 20 that leaves 15: 1 part = 3, giving 6 footballs, 15 cricket balls and 36 shuttlecocks.
s: Finds 1 part = 2.8 and 5.6 footballs
Explains the cricket balls must be a multiple of 5
Gives 15 cricket balls with 6 footballs and 36 shuttlecocks

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 4 : 6 : 10 :: 6 : 9 : 15.
Statement 2: If 2 : 3 : 5 :: p : q : 20, then p + q = 20.
Statement 3: Adding 1 to every term of 8 : 4 : 2 : 1 gives 9 : 5 : 3 : 2, which is proportional to it.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q:
A recipe card lists jaggery : wheat flour : ghee = 2 : 5 : 1. Ravi copies it as wheat flour : ghee : jaggery = 5 : 2 : 1.
(a) What did Ravi get wrong?
(b) Write the ratio correctly in Ravi's order, and use it to find the wheat flour and jaggery for 3 cups of ghee.
questions.a: (a) He changed the order of the quantities but did not move the numbers with them, so his card now says 2 parts of ghee and 1 part of jaggery, which is wrong. (b) Wheat flour : ghee : jaggery = 5 : 1 : 2. 3 cups of ghee is 3 times 1, so wheat flour = 15 cups and jaggery = 6 cups.
s: Part (a): the numbers were not moved with their quantities
Part (b): 5 : 1 : 2, giving 15 cups of flour and 6 cups of jaggery

questions.q:
A garam masala recipe uses cumin : coriander : pepper : cardamom = 4 : 6 : 2 : 1 (in spoons). Three caterers report their batches. Each caterer measured cumin, coriander and pepper with a level spoon, but Caterer B added the cardamom by guesswork.
Caterer A: 10 : 15 : 5 : 2.5
Caterer B: 6 : 9 : 3 : 2
Caterer C: 2 : 3 : 1 : 0.5
(a) Test each batch against the recipe term by term.
(b) By what common factor do Caterer B's cumin, coriander and pepper scale the recipe, and how much cardamom should B have used?
(c) How many times as big as Caterer C's batch is Caterer A's?
(d) Find the amounts of all four spices for a batch that uses 9 spoons of pepper.
(e) Caterer C must now make a batch of 19.5 spoons in all, in the recipe ratio. Find the amount of each spice.
questions.a: (a) A: 10 / 4 = 15 / 6 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 / 1 = 2.5, proportional. B: 6 / 4 = 9 / 6 = 3 / 2 = 1.5, but 2 / 1 = 2, not proportional. C: every quotient is 0.5, proportional. (b) The factor is 1.5, so B should have used 1.5 x 1 = 1.5 spoons of cardamom (B used 0.5 spoon too much). (c) 2.5 / 0.5 = 5 times (totals 32.5 and 6.5 spoons). (d) Pepper's term is 2, so the factor is 9 / 2 = 4.5: cumin 18, coriander 27, pepper 9, cardamom 4.5 spoons. (e) The terms add to 13, so 1 part = 19.5 / 13 = 1.5 spoons: cumin 6, coriander 9, pepper 3, cardamom 1.5 spoons.
s: Part (a): A and C proportional, B not, with the quotients
Part (b): factor 1.5, so 1.5 spoons of cardamom
Part (c): 5 times
Part (e): 6, 9, 3 and 1.5 spoons

questions.q: A cook's recipe uses three spices in the ratio 12 : 9 : 6. Four helpers make their own batches. Which batch is NOT proportional to 12 : 9 : 6?

A potting mix uses soil : compost : sand = 3 : 2 : 1 by weight. Meena has 5 kg of compost.
(a) How much soil and sand does she need to use all the compost?
(b) She packs the whole mix into 2 kg bags. How many bags can she fill completely?
questions.a: (a) 5 kg of compost is 2 parts, so 1 part = 2.5 kg: soil 3 x 2.5 = 7.5 kg, sand 2.5 kg. (b) Total = 7.5 + 5 + 2.5 = 15 kg. 15 / 2 = 7.5, so she fills 7 bags completely (1 kg is left over).
s: Part (a): 7.5 kg soil and 2.5 kg sand
Part (b): 15 kg in all, so 7 full bags

questions.q:
A handloom cooperative in Pochampally makes a green dye from blue powder : yellow powder : salt = 3 : 4 : 1 by weight. The salt is weighed on an electronic scale and is always right; the two powders are scooped by hand. The dye register shows:
Batch 1: 45 g blue, 60 g yellow, 15 g salt
Batch 2: 36 g blue, 48 g yellow, 15 g salt
Batch 3: 27 g blue, 36 g yellow, 9 g salt
(a) Which batch breaks the ratio?
(b) Taking the salt as correct, how much blue and yellow should that batch have had, and what would its total weight then be?
(c) A sack holds 1.2 kg of yellow powder. How much blue and salt are needed to use it all, and how much dye will that make?
(d) Suppose instead the blue scoop had been the trusted measurement for that batch. What would then be wrong with it, and by how much? Why must the register say which entry is trusted?
questions.a: (a) Batch 2: blue 36 / 3 = 12 and yellow 48 / 4 = 12, but salt 15 / 1 = 15. Batches 1 and 3 give 15 and 9 for every term. (b) Salt 15 g is 1 part, so blue = 45 g and yellow = 60 g (9 g and 12 g short), total 45 + 60 + 15 = 120 g. (c) 1,200 g of yellow is 4 parts, so 1 part = 300 g: blue 900 g, salt 300 g, total 2,400 g = 2.4 kg of dye. (d) Blue 36 g would make 1 part = 12 g, so the salt should be 12 g and Batch 2 would have 3 g too much salt. The same entry gives two different fixes, so without knowing which amount is trusted the error cannot be named.
s: Part (a): Batch 2, salt factor 15 against 12 for the powders
Part (b): 45 g blue and 60 g yellow, total 120 g
Part (c): 900 g blue and 300 g salt, 2.4 kg of dye
Part (d): salt 3 g too much, so the trusted entry decides the fix

questions.q: For the concrete ratio cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 1.5 : 3, batch P used 4 : 6 : 12 bags and batch Q used 3 : 5.5 : 13.5 bags. Neha claims: 'Both batches use 22 bags in all, so both are the same mix as 1 : 1.5 : 3.' Is she right? Test each batch term by term.
questions.a: No, Neha is wrong. Both totals are 22 bags, but P: 4 / 1 = 6 / 1.5 = 12 / 3 = 4, so P is proportional to 1 : 1.5 : 3. Q: 3 / 1 = 3, 5.5 / 1.5 = 3.67 and 13.5 / 3 = 4.5, not the same factor, so Q is a different mix (too much gravel). Equal totals say nothing about the ratio; every term must change by the same factor.
s: Verdict: No, the claim is wrong
Shows P has factor 4 for every term
Shows Q's factors differ, so equal totals do not mean the same ratio

questions.q:
A school library has 1,260 science books in the ratio Physics : Chemistry : Biology = 4 : 3 : 2.
(a) How many Biology books are there?
(b) Using part (a), how many more Physics books than Biology books are there?
questions.a: (a) Sum of terms = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. Biology = 1,260 x 2 / 9 = 280 books. (b) Physics = 1,260 x 4 / 9 = 560, which is twice the Biology count, so there are 560 - 280 = 280 more Physics books.
s: Part (a): 280 Biology books
Part (b): 560 Physics books, so 280 more

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: To divide 72 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4, divide 72 by 3, the number of terms, and multiply each term by the result.
Statement 2: Dividing Rs 600 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 gives the same three shares as dividing it in the ratio 0.5 : 1 : 1.5.
Statement 3: When 3 hours are divided in the ratio 5 : 3 : 4, the longest part is 1 hour 15 minutes and the shortest part is 1 hour.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only

questions.q: Rs 4,950 is shared among three cousins in the ratio 1.5 : 2 : 1. What is the smallest share?

Three women of a self-help group in Kutch run a small pickle unit. They agree to share each month's profit in the ratio of the hours each one works. In March, Asha worked 60 hours, Bina 45 hours and Chitra 75 hours, and the profit was Rs 27,000.
(a) Write the ratio of their hours in simplest form.
(b) Find each woman's share of the March profit.
(c) Bina suggests sharing the profit equally instead. Who would gain, who would lose, and by how much?
(d) The group keeps sharing by hours and adds a rule that no one should get less than Rs 7,000 in a month. Does Bina's March share meet the rule? With the same hours, what is the smallest monthly profit for which it is met?
questions.a: (a) 60 : 45 : 75; the HCF is 15, so 4 : 3 : 5. (b) Sum = 12. Asha 27,000 x 4 / 12 = Rs 9,000, Bina 27,000 x 3 / 12 = Rs 6,750, Chitra 27,000 x 5 / 12 = Rs 11,250. (c) An equal share is 27,000 / 3 = Rs 9,000. Asha gets the same, Bina gains Rs 2,250 and Chitra loses Rs 2,250. (d) No: Rs 6,750 is less than Rs 7,000. Bina gets 3/12 of the profit, so the profit must be at least 7,000 x 12 / 3 = Rs 28,000.
s: Part (b): Rs 9,000, Rs 6,750 and Rs 11,250
Part (c): Bina gains and Chitra loses Rs 2,250 each, Asha unchanged
Part (d): March fails (Rs 6,750); the profit must be at least Rs 28,000

questions.q: Explain why no triangle can have its sides in the ratio 2 : 3 : 6, whatever lengths are chosen.
questions.a: If the sides are 2k, 3k and 6k for some length k, the two shorter sides add up to 2k + 3k = 5k, which is less than the longest side 6k. In a triangle the sum of any two sides must be more than the third side, so these lengths can never close into a triangle, for any value of k.
s: Writes the sides as 2k, 3k, 6k and finds 2k + 3k = 5k is less than 6k
Uses the rule that two sides must add to more than the third, for every k

questions.q:
Assertion (A): When Rs 1,350 is shared among three friends in the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 2, the largest share is Rs 600.
Reason (R): A ratio can be used to divide a quantity only when all its terms are whole numbers.
questions.a: A is true but R is false
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true

questions.q:
A carpenter cuts a 2.4 m plank into three pieces in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5 and plans to join them into a triangular frame.
(a) Find the length of each piece.
(b) Show that the frame cannot be made.
(c) He cuts a new 2.4 m plank in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 instead. Find the pieces and show that this frame can be made.
questions.a: (a) Sum = 8, so the pieces are 2.4 x 1 / 8 = 0.3 m, 2.4 x 2 / 8 = 0.6 m and 2.4 x 5 / 8 = 1.5 m. (b) 0.3 + 0.6 = 0.9 m, which is less than 1.5 m, so the two short pieces cannot reach the ends of the long piece. (c) Sum = 12: 0.6 m, 0.8 m and 1.0 m. 0.6 + 0.8 = 1.4 m is more than 1.0 m (and the other pairs are larger still), so the frame can be made.
s: Part (a): 0.3 m, 0.6 m and 1.5 m
Part (b): 0.9 m is less than 1.5 m
Part (c): 0.6 m, 0.8 m and 1.0 m, with 1.4 m more than 1.0 m

questions.q: A 2.5 km relay is split among five runners in the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 2 : 2.5 : 3, in running order. The last runner covers ___ metres. (Write the number in digits.)
A school stall sold 60 snacks: samosas at Rs 10, biscuit packets at Rs 5 and toffees at Rs 2. The numbers sold were in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 in that order. How much money did the stall take?
questions.a: Rs 260

questions.q:
A temple donation box holds 180 coins. The numbers of Rs 10, Rs 5, Rs 2 and Rs 1 coins are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 6.
(a) Find the number of coins of each kind.
(b) Find the money given by each kind of coin and the total money in the box.
(c) Which kind of coin gives the most money, and which kind is the most numerous?
(d) The trustee writes that the money in the box is also in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 6. Show that this is wrong, and write the ratio of the money in simplest form.
questions.a: (a) Sum = 15. Rs 10: 180 x 2 / 15 = 24; Rs 5: 36; Rs 2: 48; Rs 1: 72. (b) Rs 240, Rs 180, Rs 96 and Rs 72; total Rs 588. (c) The Rs 10 coins give the most money (Rs 240) even though the Rs 1 coins are the most numerous (72). (d) The money is 240 : 180 : 96 : 72. Dividing by the HCF 12 gives 20 : 15 : 8 : 6, not 2 : 3 : 4 : 6. The numbers of coins are in 2 : 3 : 4 : 6, but each coin has a different value, so the money is not.
s: Part (a): 24, 36, 48 and 72 coins
Part (b): Rs 240, 180, 96, 72 and total Rs 588
Part (c): Rs 10 coins give most money, Rs 1 coins are most numerous
Part (d): money ratio 20 : 15 : 8 : 6, so the trustee is wrong

questions.q: True or False: Dividing 72 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and dividing 72 in the ratio 2 : 4 : 6 give exactly the same three parts. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. 72 in 1 : 2 : 3 (sum 6) gives 12, 24 and 36. 72 in 2 : 4 : 6 (sum 12) gives 72 x 2 / 12 = 12, 24 and 36. The ratio 2 : 4 : 6 is just 1 : 2 : 3 with every term doubled, so each term and the sum double together and every fraction term / sum stays the same.
s: States True
Shows both give 12, 24, 36, or explains that term / sum is unchanged

questions.q: Ishaan claims: 'Sharing Rs 1,800 in the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 2.5 gives exactly the same three shares as sharing it in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5, and in both the largest share equals the other two shares put together.' Check both parts of his claim.
questions.a: Ishaan is right. 1 : 1.5 : 2.5 has sum 5, so the shares are 1,800 x 1 / 5 = Rs 360, Rs 540 and Rs 900. 2 : 3 : 5 has sum 10, so the shares are 1,800 x 2 / 10 = Rs 360, Rs 540 and Rs 900, the same, because 2 : 3 : 5 is 1 : 1.5 : 2.5 with every term doubled. And 360 + 540 = 900, because the largest term equals the sum of the other two (2.5 = 1 + 1.5).
s: Finds the same shares from 2 : 3 : 5 and gives the doubling reason
Shows 360 + 540 = 900 and gives the verdict: right in both parts

questions.q:
Match the ratio of the angles of a triangle in Column A with its largest angle in Column B.
Column A: (1) 1 : 2 : 3 (2) 2 : 3 : 4 (3) 1 : 4 : 7 (4) 3 : 5 : 10
Column B: (a) 80 degrees (b) 105 degrees (c) 90 degrees (d) 100 degrees

A 90 cm ribbon is cut into three pieces in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.
(a) Find the length of each piece.
(b) The longest piece is then cut into two equal halves. Write the ratio of the four pieces in simplest form, in the order: first piece, second piece, then the two halves of the third piece.
questions.a: (a) Sum = 9, so the pieces are 90 x 2 / 9 = 20 cm, 30 cm and 40 cm. (b) The 40 cm piece becomes two 20 cm pieces, so the four pieces are 20 : 30 : 20 : 20, which is 2 : 3 : 2 : 2 after dividing by the HCF 10.
s: Part (a): 20 cm, 30 cm and 40 cm

questions.q:
A juice shop in Shillong sells a 'tropical mix' of mango : pineapple : orange juice = 2.5 : 1.5 : 1. Its costs per 100 ml are: mango Rs 30, pineapple Rs 40, orange Rs 20.
(a) How much mango juice is in a 750 ml glass?
(b) A customer's glass had 120 ml of orange juice. What was the size of the glass?
(c) What does the juice in a 750 ml glass cost the shop?
(d) The owner wants the juice in a 750 ml glass to cost the shop less than Rs 230, and mango must stay strictly the largest part. She is choosing between the ratios 3 : 1 : 1 and 2 : 1 : 2. Which one should she choose? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Sum = 5, so mango = 750 x 2.5 / 5 = 375 ml. (b) Orange is 1 part out of 5, so 120 ml is one-fifth of the glass: 120 x 5 = 600 ml. (c) Mango 375 ml, pineapple 750 x 1.5 / 5 = 225 ml, orange 150 ml. Cost = 3.75 x 30 + 2.25 x 40 + 1.5 x 20 = 112.5 + 90 + 30 = Rs 232.50. (d) 3 : 1 : 1 gives 450, 150, 150 ml, costing 135 + 60 + 30 = Rs 225, below Rs 230, with mango the largest. 2 : 1 : 2 gives 300, 150, 300 ml, costing 90 + 60 + 60 = Rs 210, but mango (300 ml) is no longer larger than orange (300 ml). So she should choose 3 : 1 : 1.
s: Part (a): 375 ml of mango
Part (b): a 600 ml glass
Part (c): Rs 232.50
Part (d): 3 : 1 : 1, since it costs Rs 225 and keeps mango largest, while 2 : 1 : 2 ties mango with orange

questions.q:
Riya plans 3 hours of study for Maths, Science and English in the ratio 2.5 : 2 : 1.5.
(a) How many minutes does she give to each subject?
(b) She then adds 30 minutes to English only. Is her new plan still in the ratio 2.5 : 2 : 1.5? Show why.
questions.a: (a) 3 hours = 180 minutes; sum of terms = 6. Maths 180 x 2.5 / 6 = 75 min, Science 60 min, English 45 min. (b) The new times are 75 : 60 : 75. Maths and Science are unchanged but English grew from 45 to 75, so not every term changed by the same factor (75 / 45 is not 1). The ratio is no longer 2.5 : 2 : 1.5.
s: Part (a): 75, 60 and 45 minutes
Part (b): 75 : 60 : 75 is not proportional to 2.5 : 2 : 1.5

questions.q: Two partners share a profit of Rs 84,000 in the ratio 3 : 4. After sharing, the second partner gives Rs 6,000 of her share to the first. In what ratio is the profit now held?

A school geometry club is making triangle cards.
(a) Find the angles of a triangle whose angles are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3, and of one whose angles are in the ratio 2 : 2 : 5.
(b) Name each triangle in part (a) by its largest angle (acute, right or obtuse).
(c) A card must show sides in the ratio 4 : 5 : 8 or 2 : 3 : 5. Which of these two side ratios can actually be drawn? Justify.
(d) For the side ratio that works, find the sides if the perimeter is 34 cm.
(e) Will every triangle in that side ratio with a perimeter of 34 cm be congruent to your triangle in part (d)? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 1 : 2 : 3 (sum 6): 30, 60, 90 degrees. 2 : 2 : 5 (sum 9): 40, 40, 100 degrees. (b) The first is right-angled, the second is obtuse-angled. (c) 4 : 5 : 8 works, since 4k + 5k = 9k is more than 8k. 2 : 3 : 5 does not, since 2k + 3k = 5k only equals the longest side, so the sides lie flat. (d) Sum = 17: 34 x 4 / 17 = 8 cm, 10 cm and 16 cm. (e) Yes. Fixing the perimeter fixes the three lengths at 8, 10 and 16 cm, and triangles with the same three sides are congruent. Without a fixed perimeter they need not be.
s: Part (a): 30, 60, 90 and 40, 40, 100 degrees
Part (b): right-angled and obtuse-angled
Part (c): 4 : 5 : 8 can be drawn, 2 : 3 : 5 cannot
Part (d): 8 cm, 10 cm and 16 cm
Part (e): yes, because the three sides are now fixed

questions.q:
A quiz prize is shared among three winners in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7, and the largest share is Rs 840.
(a) Find the total prize.
(b) If the same prize had been shared equally, how much less would the winner of the largest share have got?
questions.a: (a) The largest share is 7 parts, so 1 part = 840 / 7 = Rs 120. The terms add to 12, so the prize is 12 x 120 = Rs 1,440. (b) An equal share is 1,440 / 3 = Rs 480, so she would have got 840 - 480 = Rs 360 less.
s: Part (a): 1 part = Rs 120, prize Rs 1,440
Part (b): equal share Rs 480, so Rs 360 less

questions.q: A 2-hour dance rehearsal is split as warm-up : new steps : full run : rest = 2 : 5 : 4 : 1. How long is the full run?
questions.a: 40 minutes

questions.q:
Three friends share a cab fare of Rs 1,800 in the ratio of the distances they travelled, 4.5 : 3 : 1.5.
(a) Find each friend's share.
(b) Write the ratio 4.5 : 3 : 1.5 in its simplest whole-number form.
(c) The fare rises by Rs 600. The friend who travelled least says each should pay Rs 200 more. Using part (b), find what each should really pay extra.
questions.a: (a) Sum = 9. Shares: 1,800 x 4.5 / 9 = Rs 900, 1,800 x 3 / 9 = Rs 600, 1,800 x 1.5 / 9 = Rs 300. (b) Multiply by 2 to get 9 : 6 : 3, then divide by the HCF 3: 3 : 2 : 1. (c) The extra Rs 600 is shared in 3 : 2 : 1 (sum 6): Rs 300, Rs 200 and Rs 100. Only the second friend's extra is Rs 200; the friend who travelled least should pay only Rs 100 more.
s: Part (a): Rs 900, Rs 600 and Rs 300
Part (c): extra Rs 300, Rs 200 and Rs 100

questions.q: True or False: In a pie chart showing the favourite games of 60 students, a sector of 60 degrees must stand for 60 students. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. The whole 360 degrees stands for all 60 students, so each degree stands for 60 / 360 = 1/6 of a student. A 60 degree sector stands for 60 x 60 / 360 = 10 students. The angle equals the number of students only when the total is 360.
s: States False
Finds 60 x 60 / 360 = 10 students

questions.q: In a survey, 240 students named their favourite sport: cricket 90, football 60, kabaddi 50 and badminton 40. What angle should the kabaddi sector have in a pie chart?
questions.a: 75 degrees

questions.q:
A pie chart of the lunch choices in one class has a rice sector of 150 degrees and a roti sector of 120 degrees; the rest of the circle is noodles. 25 students chose rice.
(a) How many students are in the class?
(b) Find the angle of the noodles sector and the number of students who chose noodles.
(c) Write the ratio rice : roti : noodles (in students) in simplest form.
questions.a: (a) 150 degrees stands for 25 students, so 360 degrees stands for 25 x 360 / 150 = 60 students. (b) Noodles = 360 - 150 - 120 = 90 degrees, which is 60 x 90 / 360 = 15 students. (c) Roti = 60 x 120 / 360 = 20 students. 25 : 20 : 15 = 5 : 4 : 3 (dividing by the HCF 5).
s: Part (a): 60 students
Part (b): 90 degrees and 15 students

questions.q: A family's monthly budget is shown in a pie chart: food 35%, rent 25%, education 20%, savings 12%, others 8%. How many degrees larger is the food sector than the education sector?
questions.a: 54 degrees

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Data in the ratio 12 : 10 : 8 : 6 : 4 gives the same pie-chart angles as data in the ratio 6 : 5 : 4 : 3 : 2.
Statement 2: A category that makes up 15% of the data gets a sector of 15 degrees.
Statement 3: A pie chart can have sectors of 120, 90, 60, 60 and 40 degrees.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only

questions.q:
A ward committee in Jaipur asked 600 households to name the biggest problem in their area. The replies were: water supply 210, roads 150, garbage 135, streetlights 60, other 45.
(a) Find the pie-chart angle for each reply.
(b) What percentage of households named garbage?
(c) The committee will fund problems starting from the largest sector, and stop as soon as the funded sectors together make at least half the pie. Which problems are funded?
(d) Rs 9 lakh is shared between the funded problems in the ratio of the number of households that named them. How much does each get?
questions.a: (a) Each household is 360 / 600 = 0.6 degree. Water 126, roads 90, garbage 81, streetlights 36, other 27 degrees (total 360). (b) 135 / 600 x 100 = 22.5%. (c) Water alone is 126 degrees, less than half (180 degrees). Water and roads together are 126 + 90 = 216 degrees, which is at least 180, so water supply and roads are funded. (d) 210 : 150 = 7 : 5. Water gets 9,00,000 x 7 / 12 = Rs 5,25,000 and roads 9,00,000 x 5 / 12 = Rs 3,75,000.
s: Part (a): 126, 90, 81, 36 and 27 degrees
Part (c): water supply and roads (216 degrees)

questions.q: A pie chart shows the main cooking fuel of 720 households: LPG 210 degrees, firewood 75 degrees, biogas 45 degrees, electricity 30 degrees. How many households use firewood?
questions.a: 150 households

questions.q:
480 people named their favourite fruit: mango 200, banana 120, apple 100 and guava 60.
(a) Write the ratio mango : banana : apple : guava in simplest form.
(b) Use part (a) to find the pie-chart angle for each fruit.
questions.a: (a) The HCF of 200, 120, 100 and 60 is 20, so the ratio is 10 : 6 : 5 : 3. (b) Sum = 24, and 360 / 24 = 15 degrees per part. Mango 150, banana 90, apple 75 and guava 45 degrees.
s: Part (b): 150, 90, 75 and 45 degrees

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a pie chart, a category that has 15% of the data gets a sector of 54 degrees, not 15 degrees.
Reason (R): Each 1% of the data takes up 3.6 degrees of the circle, because the whole 360 degrees stands for 100%.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q:
A school uses 2,000 litres of water a day: drinking 15%, toilets 40%, kitchen 25%, garden 20%.
(a) Find the pie-chart angle for each use.
(b) Using the garden sector's angle, find how many litres the garden gets.
questions.a: (a) Angle = percentage / 100 x 360. Drinking 54, toilets 144, kitchen 90, garden 72 degrees. (b) 72 / 360 = 1/5, and 2,000 / 5 = 400 litres.
s: Part (a): 54, 144, 90 and 72 degrees
Part (b): 400 litres

questions.q: Simran claims: 'If two pie charts from two different surveys both show a 90 degree sector for cricket, then the same number of students chose cricket in both surveys.' Is Simran right? Support your answer with numbers.
questions.a: No, Simran is wrong. A 90 degree sector is one-quarter of the circle, so it shows one-quarter of that survey's total, not a fixed number. In a survey of 40 students it stands for 40 x 90 / 360 = 10 students; in a survey of 120 students it stands for 30 students. The same angle means the same fraction, and the numbers are equal only when the totals are equal.
s: Verdict: No
Explains that 90 degrees is one-quarter of each survey's total
Gives two totals with different counts, such as 10 and 30 students

questions.q: In a pie chart, a sector of 54 degrees stands for 27 students. The whole chart stands for ___ students. (Write the number in digits.)

120 students of a school said how they reach school: walk 42, cycle 30, bus 24, auto 15, car 9.
(a) Find the pie-chart angle for each mode.
(b) Check that your angles make a full circle, and find the percentage of students who cycle.
(c) Next term, 10 students who walked start cycling (the total stays 120). Find the new angles for walk and cycle.
(d) A teacher reads the bus sector of 72 degrees and says '72 students come by bus.' Correct her.
(e) Instead, suppose 12 new students join the school and all of them walk. Explain why the bus sector would get smaller even though the same 24 students still come by bus, and find its new angle to one decimal place.
questions.a: (a) Each student is 360 / 120 = 3 degrees. Walk 126, cycle 90, bus 72, auto 45, car 27 degrees. (b) 126 + 90 + 72 + 45 + 27 = 360 degrees. Cycle: 30 / 120 x 100 = 25%. (c) Walk 32 x 3 = 96 degrees, cycle 40 x 3 = 120 degrees. (d) 72 degrees is 72 / 360 = 1/5 of the circle, so it stands for 120 / 5 = 24 students, not 72. (e) The angle shows the fraction of the whole. With 132 students, 24 is a smaller fraction: 24 / 132 x 360 = 65.5 degrees (about).
s: Part (a): 126, 90, 72, 45 and 27 degrees
Part (b): total 360 degrees, 25% cycle
Part (c): walk 96 and cycle 120 degrees
Part (d): the bus sector stands for 24 students, not 72
Part (e): the total grew, so the fraction falls; about 65.5 degrees

questions.q:
A pie chart shows how Kabir spends a 24-hour day: sleep 1/3, school 1/4, play 1/8, homework 1/12, and the rest on other things.
(a) Find the angle of the 'other things' sector.
(b) How many hours does Kabir spend on other things?
s: Part (a): 5/24 of the day, 75 degrees
Part (b): 5 hours

questions.q: A pie chart of the ice-cream flavours sold one day has sectors of 144, 108, 72 and 36 degrees. In what ratio were the four flavours sold?
A pie chart of the TV channels a group of viewers like best has three sectors. News measures 54 degrees and Sports 90 degrees. What percentage of the viewers chose the third sector, Entertainment?

A newspaper prints a pie chart of how a city handles its 1,200 tonnes of waste a day. The labels read: recycled 30%, composted 25%, sent to landfill 40%, burnt 10%.
(a) Show that these labels cannot all be correct. If only one label is wrong, what would each label have to be in turn?
(b) The city's weighbridge records 420 tonnes going to landfill each day. Which label was wrong?
(c) What angle should the composted sector have?
(d) The city wants the landfill sector to be at most 90 degrees. Plan 1 moves 120 tonnes a day from landfill to composting; Plan 2 burns 100 more tonnes a day taken from landfill. Which plan meets the target? Justify with angles.
questions.a: (a) 30 + 25 + 40 + 10 = 105%, but a pie chart must make exactly 100% (360 degrees). The single wrong label must be 5 points too high: recycled 25%, or composted 20%, or landfill 35%, or burnt 5%. (b) 420 / 1,200 x 100 = 35%, so the landfill label (40%) was wrong. (c) 25% of 360 = 90 degrees. (d) Plan 1 leaves 420 - 120 = 300 tonnes, 300 / 1,200 x 360 = 90 degrees, which meets 'at most 90'. Plan 2 leaves 320 tonnes, 320 / 1,200 x 360 = 96 degrees, which does not. So Plan 1.
s: Part (a): 105%, and the four possible single corrections
Part (b): 35%, so the landfill label
Part (c): 90 degrees
Part (d): Plan 1 (90 degrees) meets the target, Plan 2 (96 degrees) does not

questions.q: Data about 120 people is 50 tea drinkers, 40 coffee drinkers and 30 who drink neither. A student draws the sectors at 50, 40 and 30 degrees. Explain what goes wrong with her chart, and give the correct angles.
questions.a: Her sectors add up to only 120 degrees, so 240 degrees of the circle are left empty and the chart does not show the whole. The angles must be fractions of 360 degrees: each person is 360 / 120 = 3 degrees, so tea 150, coffee 120 and neither 90 degrees.
s: Explains that the sectors fill only 120 of the 360 degrees
Gives 150, 120 and 90 degrees

questions.q: A pie chart about the 90 trees in a school campus has sectors of 160, 100, 60 and 40 degrees. Name four kinds of trees for the sectors, find how many trees each sector stands for, and check that your numbers give back the angles.
questions.a: Example: neem 160, mango 100, ashoka 60, peepal 40 degrees. Each degree stands for 90 / 360 = 0.25 tree, so the counts are 40 neem, 25 mango, 15 ashoka and 10 peepal (total 90). Check: 40 / 90 x 360 = 160, 25 / 90 x 360 = 100, 15 / 90 x 360 = 60, 10 / 90 x 360 = 40 degrees. (Any four tree names earn the mark.)
s: Names four categories for the four sectors
Finds 40, 25, 15 and 10 trees
Checks each count gives back its angle

questions.q:
Match each percentage of the data in Column A with its pie-chart angle in Column B.
Column A: (1) 5% (2) 12.5% (3) 30% (4) 45%
Column B: (a) 108 degrees (b) 18 degrees (c) 162 degrees (d) 45 degrees

Two schools made pie charts of their students' favourite subject. School A has 400 students and its Maths sector is 90 degrees. School B has 200 students and its Maths sector is 126 degrees.
(a) How many students chose Maths in each school?
(b) What percentage of each school chose Maths?
(c) Which school has more students who chose Maths?
(d) The district wants to reward the school that is more 'Maths-friendly'. Which school should it pick, and why would counting students mislead?
(e) How many more students in School A would have to choose Maths for its share to equal School B's?
questions.a: (a) A: 400 x 90 / 360 = 100 students. B: 200 x 126 / 360 = 70 students. (b) A: 90 / 360 = 25%. B: 126 / 360 = 35%. (c) School A (100 against 70). (d) School B: 35% of its students chose Maths against 25% in School A. School A's bigger count comes only from its being twice as big; the share, which the sector angle shows, compares the schools fairly. (e) 35% of 400 = 140 students, so 140 - 100 = 40 more.
s: Part (a): 100 and 70 students
Part (b): 25% and 35%
Part (c): School A has more Maths students
Part (d): School B, by share, since A's count reflects its size
Part (e): 40 more students

questions.q: Five workers can paint a school boundary wall in 6 days. Arun says: '6 workers will take 5 days, and 10 workers will take 1 day, because 10 is 5 more than 5, so I take 5 days off.' Assume every worker paints at the same rate. Check both parts of Arun's statement.
questions.a: Arun is partly right. Workers and days are in inverse proportion, so workers x days stays 5 x 6 = 30. For 6 workers, 30 / 6 = 5 days, so the first part is correct. For 10 workers, 30 / 10 = 3 days, not 1 day. Doubling the workers halves the days; subtracting the increase in workers from the days is not how inverse proportion works.
s: Uses workers x days = 30 and confirms 5 days for 6 workers
Finds 3 days for 10 workers
Verdict partly right, with the reason the subtraction is wrong

questions.q: A student records four tables of x and y. In which table are x and y in inverse proportion?

x and y are in inverse proportion. The table shows some of their values:
x: 8, 12, ?, 40
y: 30, ?, 16, ?
(a) Find the constant k = xy.
(b) Fill in the three missing values.
s: Part (a): k = 240
Part (b): 20, 15 and 6

questions.q: 15 workers can build a wall in 12 days. Working at the same rate, 20 workers can build the same wall in ___ days. (Write the number in digits.)

A relief camp in Assam has food stocks for 400 people for 18 days. All people eat the same amount each day.
(a) If 100 more people arrive on the first day, how long will the food last?
(b) If the food must last 24 days, how many people can the camp feed?
(c) Copy and complete the pattern: 200 people, ? days; 300 people, ? days; 600 people, ? days; 900 people, ? days.
(d) The next food delivery comes in 15 days. A group of 90 people asks to join the 400 already in the camp. Can the camp accept all of them without running out before the delivery? Justify.
questions.a: (a) People x days stays 400 x 18 = 7,200. 7,200 / 500 = 14.4 days. (b) 7,200 / 24 = 300 people. (c) 7,200 / 200 = 36, 7,200 / 300 = 24, 7,200 / 600 = 12, 7,200 / 900 = 8 days. (d) To last 15 days the camp can feed at most 7,200 / 15 = 480 people. 400 + 90 = 490 is more than 480, so it cannot accept all 90 (at most 80 more).
s: Part (a): 14.4 days
Part (b): 300 people
Part (c): 36, 24, 12 and 8 days
Part (d): no, only 480 people can be fed for 15 days

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: If x and y are in inverse proportion and x increases by 3, then y decreases by 3.
Statement 2: If 8 taps fill a tank in 6 hours, then 4 such taps fill it in 3 hours, because the taps and the hours are in proportion.
Statement 3: The number of pages in a book and the time needed to read it at a fixed reading speed are in direct proportion.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only

questions.q:
A toy factory needs 36 machines to complete an order in 45 days. All machines work at the same rate.
(a) How many days would 54 machines take, and how many machines would finish the order in 27 days?
(b) The buyer now wants the order in 30 days. How many extra machines are needed?
(c) The factory can buy the extra machines at Rs 2,50,000 each, or rent them at Rs 4,000 per machine per day for the 30 days. For this order alone, which is cheaper, and by how much?
(d) State one assumption you made in parts (a) and (b), and say what would happen to your answer to (b) if it were false.
questions.a: (a) Machines x days = 36 x 45 = 1,620, so 54 machines take 1,620 / 54 = 30 days, and 1,620 / 27 = 60 machines finish in 27 days. (b) 1,620 / 30 = 54 machines, so 54 - 36 = 18 extra machines. (c) Buying: 18 x 2,50,000 = Rs 45,00,000. Renting: 18 x 30 x 4,000 = Rs 21,60,000. Renting is cheaper by Rs 23,40,000. (d) Assumption: every machine, including the extra ones, works at the same rate for the same hours each day (the quantities are inversely proportional). If the extra machines were slower, 18 would not be enough and more would be needed.
s: Part (a): 30 days and 60 machines
Part (b): 18 extra machines
Part (c): buying Rs 45,00,000 against renting Rs 21,60,000, so rent, cheaper by Rs 23,40,000
Part (d): names the same-rate assumption and its effect

questions.q:
A milk dairy in Anand packs 6,000 pouches every morning. Machine P alone packs all of them in 4 hours and machine Q alone in 6 hours. Packing starts at 6:00 am.
(a) How many pouches does each machine pack in one hour?
(b) If both machines run together, at what time will packing finish?
(c) One morning Q breaks down. The pouches must be packed by 8:30 am so the vans can load. The manager can start P alone early at 4:30 am (an extra shift costing Rs 1,500), or hire machine R for Rs 2,000, which alone packs 6,000 pouches in 5 hours, and run P and R together from 6:00 am. She wants the cheaper option that still meets the deadline. Which should she choose? Justify with times.
questions.a: (a) P: 6,000 / 4 = 1,500 pouches per hour. Q: 6,000 / 6 = 1,000 pouches per hour. (b) Together 2,500 pouches per hour, so 6,000 / 2,500 = 2.4 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes; packing finishes at 8:24 am. (c) P alone takes 6,000 / 1,500 = 4 hours, so starting at 4:30 am it finishes at 8:30 am, just meeting the deadline. R packs 6,000 / 5 = 1,200 pouches per hour, so P and R together pack 2,700 per hour and take 6,000 / 2,700 = 2.2 hours (about 2 hours 13 minutes), finishing about 8:13 am. Both meet the deadline; the early shift costs Rs 1,500 against Rs 2,000, so she should run P early.
s: Part (a): 1,500 and 1,000 pouches per hour
Part (b): 2.4 hours, finishing at 8:24 am
Part (c): both finish by 8:30 am (8:30 and about 8:13), so the cheaper early shift for P

questions.q: A small pump fills a tank in 12 hours and a large pump fills it in 4 hours. If both pumps run together, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.a: 3 hours

questions.q:
A bus depot lists the time a bus takes on one fixed route at different speeds:
speed (km/h): 40, 48, 60, 80
time (hours): 3, 2.5, 2, 1.6
(a) One time in the list is wrong. Find it, using the products of speed and time.
(b) Correct it, and state the factor by which the time changes when the speed goes from 40 to 80 km/h.
questions.a: (a) 40 x 3 = 120, 48 x 2.5 = 120, 60 x 2 = 120, but 80 x 1.6 = 128. Speed and time on a fixed route are in inverse proportion, so the product must stay 120; the time for 80 km/h is wrong. (b) 120 / 80 = 1.5 hours. The speed is multiplied by 2, so the time is multiplied by 1/2 (3 hours to 1.5 hours).
s: Part (a): products 120, 120, 120 and 128, so the 80 km/h time is wrong
Part (b): 1.5 hours, the time halves when the speed doubles

questions.q:
Assertion (A): If 3 pumps fill a tank in 20 hours, then 5 such pumps fill it in 12 hours.
Reason (R): In a direct proportion a : b :: c : d, the fourth term is d = (b x c) / a.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q:
Tap A fills a water tank in 5 hours and tap B fills it in 7.5 hours.
(a) What part of the tank does each tap fill in 1 hour?
(b) How long do the two taps take together?
(c) A function starts 3 hours after the taps are opened, and the tank must be full before those 3 hours are over. Will the two taps together manage it? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Tap A: 1/5 of the tank per hour. Tap B: 1 / 7.5 = 2/15 of the tank per hour. (b) Together: 1/5 + 2/15 = 3/15 + 2/15 = 5/15 = 1/3 of the tank per hour, so they take 3 hours. (c) No. They take exactly 3 hours, so the tank fills only as the 3 hours end, not before.
s: Part (a): 1/5 and 2/15 of the tank per hour
Part (b): 1/3 per hour, so 3 hours
Part (c): no, it takes the full 3 hours

questions.q:
Match each situation in Column A with its answer in Column B.
Column A: (1) 8 taps fill a tank in 9 hours; hours for 6 taps (2) 5 kg of rice costs Rs 340; rupees for 8 kg (3) 12 painters take 10 days; days for 8 painters (4) a school day has 8 periods of 45 minutes; minutes per period with 10 periods in the same time
Column B: (a) 15 (b) 36 (c) 12 (d) 544

Leela can paint a wall in 6 hours and Mohan can paint the same wall in 3 hours.
(a) What part of the wall do they paint together in 1 hour?
(b) Using part (a), how long do they take to paint the wall together?
questions.a: (a) Leela paints 1/6 and Mohan 1/3 of the wall in 1 hour; together 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 of the wall. (b) Work and time are directly proportional: 1/2 : 1 :: 1 : x, so x = 1 / (1/2) = 2 hours.
s: Part (a): 1/2 of the wall in 1 hour
Part (b): 2 hours

questions.q: A hostel has food for 150 students for 24 days. After 4 days, 30 students go home and the rest stay. How long will the remaining food last from then on?
questions.a: 25 days

questions.q:
A contractor in Kanpur is to lay a village road. Every worker works at the same rate and is paid Rs 600 a day. Her estimate sheet reads:
20 workers: 12 days
30 workers: 8 days
40 workers: 6 days
15 workers: 18 days
24 workers: 10 days
(a) One entry on the sheet is wrong. Find it and correct it.
(b) How many workers would be needed to finish in 7 days?
(c) What is the total wage bill with 20 workers?
(d) The village wants the road as early as possible, but the contractor can house at most 30 workers. Explain why the wage bill is the same for every correct entry on the sheet, and choose the crew.
questions.a: (a) Workers x days should stay 20 x 12 = 240. 30 x 8 = 240 and 40 x 6 = 240 and 24 x 10 = 240, but 15 x 18 = 270. 15 workers need 240 / 15 = 16 days, not 18. (b) 240 / 7 = 34.3..., so 35 workers are needed (34 would take more than 7 days). (c) 20 x 12 = 240 worker-days, and 240 x 600 = Rs 1,44,000. (d) The wage bill is (workers x days) x 600, and workers x days is always 240, so every crew costs Rs 1,44,000. Since cost does not decide, the earliest finish within the housing limit decides: 40 workers is too many, so 30 workers (8 days) is the choice.
s: Part (a): 15 workers should be 16 days
Part (b): 35 workers
Part (d): workers x days is fixed, so the cost is fixed; 30 workers, the fastest crew within the limit

questions.q:
A hall has 360 chairs set out in 24 rows of 15.
(a) If the chairs are set out in rows of 18, how many rows will there be?
(b) Can all 360 chairs be set out in full rows of 25? Use the inverse proportion to explain.
questions.a: (a) Rows x chairs per row = 24 x 15 = 360, so 360 / 18 = 20 rows. (b) No. The number of rows would be 360 / 25 = 14.4, which is not a whole number, so the last row would not be full.
s: Part (a): 20 rows
Part (b): 14.4 rows is not whole, so no

questions.q:
A worksheet labels the table below 'inverse proportion':
x: 2, 5, 10
y: 25, 10, 6

questions.q:
A school's 600-litre water tank can be filled by hose A in 30 minutes or by hose B in 20 minutes.
(a) How many litres per minute does each hose deliver?
(b) How long do both hoses take together?
(c) A third hose C fills the empty tank alone in 60 minutes. How long do all three hoses, running together from the start, take to fill it?
(d) If hose A is replaced by a second hose like A (two A hoses), how long would the filling take?
(e) Is a pair of A hoses as good as hose A and hose B together? Use (b) and (d) to decide, and find the difference in minutes.
questions.a: (a) A: 600 / 30 = 20 L per minute; B: 600 / 20 = 30 L per minute. (b) Together 50 L per minute, so 600 / 50 = 12 minutes. (c) C gives 600 / 60 = 10 L per minute, so all three give 20 + 30 + 10 = 60 L per minute, and 600 / 60 = 10 minutes. (d) Two A hoses give 40 L per minute, so 600 / 40 = 15 minutes. (e) No: the time depends on the rates, not on the number of hoses. A and B together take 12 minutes, and two A hoses take 15 minutes, 3 minutes longer.
s: Part (a): 20 and 30 litres per minute
Part (b): 12 minutes
Part (c): C gives 10 L per minute; together 60 L per minute, 10 minutes
Part (d): 15 minutes
Part (e): no, two A hoses are 3 minutes slower

questions.q: True or False: 6 machines take 15 days to make a batch of toys. Adding 4 more machines of the same kind cuts the time by 6 days, not by 4 days. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Machines and days are in inverse proportion, so machines x days stays 6 x 15 = 90. With 10 machines the batch takes 90 / 10 = 9 days, which is 15 - 9 = 6 days fewer. The days change by a factor (6/10), not by the same number as the machines.
s: States True
Finds 9 days from 6 x 15 = 10 x 9 = 90, so 6 days fewer
